source.test: 5g. PROSE: a pain-gated Achilles return (pain on two clocks, a proposed regression, a time floor)

expected.ret: 2 phases (Pain modulation, then Progressive loading), starting Monday 14 September.

ret: Pain modulation (prog/achilles-isometric, 2–6 block weeks, advancing when your pain rating the morning after the last session is at most pain 2 (no if unknown) and the days since you started the program is at least 14 days; at 6 block weeks it asks you before moving on)

3×15 straight-knee and 3×15 bent-knee Eccentric Heel Drops; add 2.5 kg after a session done in full with pain at 2/10 or less; above 5/10, propose taking 2.5 kg off; a bad morning cuts each exercise to two sets
Reads the pain you rated during the session (rated after the session); your pain rating the morning after the last session (checked in before the session; ignored once older than a day).
Starts with added load = 0 kg; written by session, owner.
Starts with flare-ups in a row = 0; written by session.

Plan:
    - if your pain rating the morning after the last session is above pain 4 (no if unknown): Eccentric Heel Drop: 3 sets of 15 reps at your added load at tempo 3-0-1-0; 3 sets of 15 reps at your added load at tempo 3-0-1-0, with 67% of the sets.
    - otherwise: Eccentric Heel Drop: 3 sets of 15 reps at your added load at tempo 3-0-1-0; 3 sets of 15 reps at your added load at tempo 3-0-1-0.

After each session:
    - if the pain you rated during the session is unknown: Leave everything as is.
    - otherwise:
      - if the pain you rated during the session is above pain 5: Propose, for your OK: set added load to (your added load minus 2.5 kg), never below 0 kg; raise flare-ups in a row by 1.
      - otherwise:
        - if every working set reached its target:
          - if the pain you rated during the session is at most pain 2: Raise added load by 2.5 kg; set flare-ups in a row to 0.
          - otherwise: Set flare-ups in a row to 0.
        - if a working set fell short: Set flare-ups in a row to 0.
        - if nothing fell short but something went unlogged: Leave everything as is.
